main_body: Two-storey timber-frame house: a large tiled roof slope (rows 0-43) over a front wall with a half-timbered upper storey and a stone-brick ground floor (rows 44-106)
top_band: Mid-brown tiled roof slope with dark tile marks, rows ~1-43 in the middle column, ending at a dark eave line at rows 44-45 with a brown band at 46-48
evidence: The roof is a large, clearly visible top slope with tile texture, as in the references. Below it a dark eave line and a brown band separate it from the wall, which is a real front face. The windows and door have dark inner edges and sills, so they read as inset. No receding side face is drawn. This matches the roof-over-wall structure of the references.

style.evidence: The whole piece uses only about 4-5 colours: a dark maroon-brown, a mid brown, a light brown and cream. The reference roofs have 5-6 steps with per-tile highlights and the walls have plaster speckle. The roof has some tile texture, but the large cream plaster panels in the upper storey are flat fills of one colour with no grain. The stone-brick base is a simple two-tone pattern. The dark outline is brown-tinted rather than pure black, which is fine. Tile information density is still clearly below the references, and the piece looks flatter and thinner next to them.
